threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the Tube' instead of just 'the Overground,' and your eyes widen at how many food spots open till 3 AM.
Heard a guy on the 36 last night bragging about stealing his mate's phone, then spent the rest of the journey texting on it. Classic.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a man serenading pigeons outside Aldi while juggling oranges. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you see a DJ spinning at a bus stop while commuters dance around waiting for buses. It’s the daily schadenfreude show.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they navigate BART delays without even flinching—grabbing a burrito instead of panicking about the time.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the bus this morning while a lady was arguing about her cat being a 'dog person.' Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars in Gràcia serve tapas, but many only do pintxos—better for a quick snack, but they miss the authenticity of the local bars.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their hesitance to use the 'tapa-tapa' method at bars—standing awkwardly instead of squeezing in like a local.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus is a reliable alternative to the Overground at rush hour. Welcome to the delays and 'no service' surprises!
Caught a group debating the best late-night food spots on the 68 last night. Turns out, the fried chicken at the end of Coldharbour Lane is still the king.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw my neighbor feeding stray cats while balancing her groceries. Only in Neukölln do everyday heroes blend in with the chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, the street artists often tag the same wall multiple times, creating layers of art that tell a story over weeks. It's like living in a gallery that evolves.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can name the taco truck near 24th street that’s been there since the 90s, not just the latest trendy spot.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus with a full mariachi band onboard yesterday. They played all the way down Van Ness. Classic San Francisco moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals eat tapas at bars. In reality, most of us prefer a quiet home-cooked meal over crowded places.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell the newbies in Gràcia—they're the ones still trying to pronounce 'Passeig de Sant Joan' without fumbling the 's'!
